opening: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Make the dry opening frame for a realistic 4-second extreme macro shot of Claire, the fictional adult Korean person in image 1. Image 1 is the authoritative reference for the same person's eye contour, eyelid crease, iris color, eyebrow hairs, skin age and texture, and dark fringe. Create one horizontal 16:9 cinematic 100 mm macro close-up on her LEFT eye (viewer-right on the reference). Camera is just off the bridge side so there is a subtle 3/4 view and a sliver of the bridge at frame-left, no other eye. The eye occupies the center of the upper half, with enough bare upper cheek below it to follow a single 12 to 16 mm tear pathway in later shots; the dark fringe crosses the upper edge without hiding the eye. The iris looks a little to frame-right. Eyelashes individually resolved; keep eyelid, lash line and upper cheek within useful focus. She is still and attentive, expression restrained and not exaggerated, with a naturally moist thin lower waterline but no pooling bead, drop, or wet track on the cheek yet. A single large soft window from frame-left, one natural catchlight and enough grazing reflection for water to be visible later. A muted dark background at the far edge. Quiet unretouched skin, tiny pores and fine hairs where a macro camera can see them. No makeup glam, extra light sources, smoothing, redness, visible text, graphic, panel, or watermark. It is a film input frame, not a beauty portrait or medical illustration.
ending: Use case: precise-object-edit. Image 1 is the exact opening frame of a locked 100 mm macro shot. Preserve its framing, eye contours and gaze, iris size, catchlight, every lash and hair, pores, gold hoop, light, and camera. Change only a very narrow short path of moisture immediately below the lower lash line. Make the end frame after exactly ONE natural transparent tear has just overflowed from the lower eyelid below the outer edge of the iris. One continuous hair-thin clear wet trace flowing gently down with gravity over the contiguous surface of the cheek, leading to a small pooled tip about one iris diameter below the lid. The tip remains on the skin, modest in scale, slightly elongated vertically, with a small window glint. The existing skin color and texture remain visible through the trace; water modifies reflection locally. Keep the line connected to the lower lid. No second bead anywhere, no stream emerging from mid-cheek, no floating water, no long trail to the bottom edge, no opaque white or blue color, no cosmetic shimmer, no redness or eye shape changes, no words. Same 1672×941 wide crop.
